# - bin_in: a certain amount of a part is stored in a certain type of bins
type: the amount of part and the amount of bins used are the same, as part always comes in units that are multiples of bin sizes.

time: # - bin_out: a certain amount of a part is retrieved from a certain type of bins
type: the amount of part and the amount of bins used are the same, as part always comes in units that are multiples of bin sizes.

time: # - end: the time when the simulation ends, or, alternatively, after which it should be aborted and all other events still in the queue are discarded
# - overstock_in: a certain amount of a part has arrived in the warehouse, but it could not be put into any bin, because all bins are full
type: the part was placed into the 'overstock', meaning that it is just lying around somewhere.

time: # - overstock_out: a certain amount of a part was taken from the overstock: this part was not in any bin, because all bins were occupied
type: so it was just lying around.

time: # - start: the time when the simulation begins
# - understock: there was not enough part in the warehouse to satisfy a warehouse_demand request.
# - warehouse_delivered: a certain amount of a part is shipped by the warehouse
# - warehouse_demand: a certain amount of a part is requested from the warehouse and needs to be taken out of the stored amount of this part
type: it then needs to be decided from which bin to take it or, if there is overstock, maybe it can be taken from there.

time: # - warehouse_in: a certain amount of a part has arrived at the warehouse and needs to be stored
type: it then needs to be decided where to put it.
